messages.author: 45a85351148578ad
messages.subject: opts legend.key.size
parts:
Hi ggploters,

 

The code bellow illustrates a strange behaviour when trying to alter the option legend.key.size to obtain a rectangular keys in the legend (check even position).

Any idea?

 

Thanks in advance,

fernando

 

library(ggplot2)

data <- data.frame(x = c(1), y = c(2), f = c("a"))

p <- qplot(x, y, colour = f, data = data)

p

p + opts(legend.key.size = unit(c(1.2, 2.4), "lines"))

 

data <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2), y = c(2, 2), f = c("a", "b"))

p %+% data

p %+% data + opts(legend.key.size = unit(c(1.2, 2.4), "lines"))

 

data <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3), y = c(2, 2, 2), f = c("a", "b", "c"))

p %+% data

p %+% data + opts(legend.key.size = unit(c(1.2, 2.4), "lines"))

 

data <- data.frame(x = c(1, 2, 3, 4), y = c(2, 2, 2, 2), f = c("a", "b", "c", "d"))

p %+% data

p %+% data + opts(legend.key.size = unit(c(1.2, 2.4), "lines"))

 

#sessionInfo()

messages.subject: Re: opts legend.key.size
parts:
Hi Fernando,

The legend.key.size specifies both height and width - you can't
specify them separately.

Hadley

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: opts legend.key.size
parts:
Hello Hadley, 
would it be too much trouble to introduce a feature to specify height and width separately? If you use both points and lines in a graph and you make those lines and points bigger is pretty difficult to figure out which line is which. And if you make the legend.key bigger you end up with a lot of unused space. So rectangular keys would be very usefull in this case.

Cheers
Luciano


2010/2/15 hadley wickham <h.wi...@gmail.com>

Hi Fernando,

The legend.key.size specifies both height and width - you can't
specify them separately.

Hadley
